newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican guerrillas say may target big business.
newsitem.headline: Mexican guerrillas say may target big business.

text.p: Leftist Mexican guerrillas said they might target some of Mexico's leading business people for attack and called for investigations into their vast fortunes, El Financiero newspaper said on Tuesday.

A commander of the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a Marxist-style armed group that has launched sneak attacks against the Mexican military and police, said certain Mexican business people might come under fire. But he said there were good capitalists who apparently could play a role in Mexico.

"If an economic project benefits the people, we're not going to affect it, but yes (we could target it) if it's taking the lion's share and only looking to speculate on the (stock) market," Commander "Francisco" told El Financiero.
EPR attacks in several Mexican states have left at least 20 dead and 34 wounded in recent months, the government says.

The rebel leader recommended investigations into the "huge fortunes" of wealthy Mexicans such as power broker and former Mexico City Mayor Carlos Hank Gonzalez, billionaire industrialist Carlos Slim and the family of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari. But he distinguished between them and other capitalists.

"There are business people in Mexico who should continue working in the country. We're not against investment in the country. That should benefit the majority of the people. But for this there should be agreements established," he said.

The EPR leader's views on capitalism came as another Mexican newspaper, Reforma, published rebel documents reportedly obtained from intelligence sources detailing a Marxist-Leninist type of command structure.

The EPR, which the government has said is the armed wing of the Clandestine Union of the People's Revolutionary Party (Procup), is run by a politburo, a central committee and other structures running down to collaborators and sympathisers at the bottom level, Reforma said.
